card.name: Shexani
card.era: Traditional (one of the older Assyrian line dances)
card.tagline: Bouncy two-step line dance shared by Assyrians and Kurds
card.profile: Sheikhani (Sexani / Shekhani) is one of the older Assyrian line dances - described as 'laid-back, albeit bouncy,' built on a two-step begun with the right foot and repeated with the left, danced with interlocked hands, the left arm bent against the back and the right arm forward against the dancer ahead (Wikipedia, Assyrian folk dance). A Folk Dance Federation source calls Sheikhani the 'national dance of the Assyrians.' It is common in Behdinan, the Kurmanji-speaking part of Iraqi Kurdistan, and is also danced by Kurdish Jews and Assyrians (The Kurdish Project), while in Kurdish music it is widely known as 'Sexani.'
card.insight: Ethnographic research on the Assyrian diaspora frames sheikhani as a key marker of Assyrian identity - 'where there's Assyrians, there's sheikhani' - even as its line-dance, hand-holding form is shared across Assyrian, Kurdish and Turkish wedding traditions (Cairn.info).
